memory_update.text: SPGI is the reference public-market leader for this node via Panjiva, maritime/trade data, and AIS expansion, but it is too large/diversified to be the main underfollowed discovery target.
DSGX is the cleanest mid-cap underfollowed software candidate for customs compliance, denied-party screening, and global trade workflow exposure.
ULS is a plausible TIC/certification discovery candidate tied to responsible sourcing, supplier audits, RBA/RMI, and product/supply-chain compliance.
SPIR should be treated as a speculative shadow candidate only; the commercial maritime data business was sold to private Kpler, so remaining exposure must be re-verified in filings.

Several highly relevant pure-play maritime intelligence assets appear private or not cleanly US-listed, including Kpler; later layers should map private-to-public supplier/customer relationships rather than forcing weak public proxies.

node: Supply-chain intelligence, vessel tracking, compliance, certification, and inspection tools
summary: Layer 1B expansion for the information/compliance layer behind policy-driven supply-chain shocks. The direct public universe is thin because several pure-play maritime intelligence vendors are private, including Kpler. The strongest US-listed reference anchor is S&P Global via Panjiva, maritime data, and AIS expansion. The more Serenity-relevant discovery lane is Descartes for customs/compliance workflow software, UL Solutions for testing/inspection/certification and responsible sourcing audits, and Spire Global as a speculative small-cap exception whose maritime exposure was materially reduced after selling its commercial maritime business to Kpler.
